LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1 WRITING SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences, part of Strand 5 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we connect ideas in sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. construct sentences using different language structures to give information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate using sentences for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension,

   Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. construct sentences using different language structures to give information,

   Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate using sentences for effective communication.

   Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to re-order jumbled up words to form correct sentences,

2. cooperate with peers to play a digital language game to drag and drop coordinating conjunctions to join parts of sentences,

3. work together to discuss new words related to the theme,

4. write the new words on flash cards for display in class,

5. build a vocabulary bank based on the new vocabulary acquired on the theme,

6. construct compound sentences using the new words acquired.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to re-order jumbled up words to form correct sentences,
2. cooperate with peers to play a digital language game to drag and drop coordinating conjunctions to join parts of sentences,
3. work together to discuss new words related to the theme,
4. write the new words on flash cards for display in class,
5. build a vocabulary bank based on the new vocabulary acquired on the theme,
6. construct compound sentences using the new words acquired.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creativity when constructing

compound sentences using the new words acquired.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is enhanced as the learner explores views when discussing the vocabulary

acquired related to the theme.

Values:
Integrity: This is enhanced as the learner displays transparency when using digital devices to play language games without

diverting to other sites.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Financial literacy: This is enhanced as the learner gets to learn about money when handling the theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of compound sentences and sentence structures to their learning in English.

Main points to remember:

1. identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension,
2. construct sentences using different language structures to give information,
3. appreciate using sentences for effective communication.
